output.meta_commit_message:
fix(bead): recover sync when two clones mint the same bead id

Concurrent clones could each allocate the same bead id and write their
own events/streams/<id>.jsonl. The resulting add/add conflict merged into
a stream with two issue_created events, which the reducer rejects, so
semantic conflict resolution failed on every retry and wedged the shared
bead store while sync workers held the sync lock.

Route conflict resolution through the core's relocating merge: allocate
relocation ids from a store-wide pool built from the config next_counter
plus every known stream id, write and stage the relocated stream, and
report "relocated duplicate beads: <old> -> <new>" in both the resolution
message and the sync log. The facade falls back to the legacy binding on
wheels that predate the new API.

Adds an end-to-end regression test in which two clones mint the same id,
the managed sync worker integrates and pushes, both beads survive, and
the worktree is left clean.

SASE_AGENT=[bbugyi200.athena.sase-f0][2]

[1]: https://github.com/sase-org/sase--beads/blob/main/pages/sase-f0/README.md
[2]: https://github.com/sase-org/sase--agents/blob/main/agents/bbugyi200.athena.sase-f0/README.md

import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Full suite is clean. Closing the bead.

Done. `sase-f0` is closed.

## What was wrong

Two clones each mint bead IDs from their own `next_counter`, so both can allocate the same ID (`sase-ey`) for different beads. Each writes `events/streams/sase-ey.jsonl`; on rebase that's an add/add conflict, and the resolver's union merge produced a stream with **two** `issue_created` events for one ID. `reduce_event_streams` rejected that, `resolve_bead_conflicts` raised, and every sync worker retried into the same error while holding the sync lock — the ~30-minute wedge.

## The fix

**Rust (`sase-core`, `crates/sase_core/src/bead/events.rs`)** — the merge now tracks per-event provenance (base / ours / theirs / both) through the union, detects duplicate creations, and relocates the loser instead of producing an unreducible stream:

- Root collision → the losing branch's whole subtree moves to a caller-supplied free ID as a new stream.
- Child collision (both sides adding `sase-ey.1` under a shared parent) → renumbered in place to the next free sibling, derived from the stream itself.
- Remaps `issue_id`, `parent_id`, dependencies, cascade/forced-descendant IDs, and re-mints every `event_id`.
- Winner is the base creation, else the older `(timestamp, event_id)` — so the result is identical whichever side git calls "ours".
- `merge_bead_event_streams` keeps its signature and still errors on duplicates; the new behavior is opt-in via `merge_bead_event_streams_with_relocation`.

**Python** — `conflict_resolver` allocates relocation IDs from a store-wide `_RelocationIds` (config `next_counter` plus every known stream ID), writes and stages the relocated stream, and reports `relocated duplicate beads: <old> -> <new>` in the resolution message and sync log. The facade falls back to the legacy binding on older wheels.

## Verification

- 5 new Rust unit tests (root relocation, orientation independence, event-ID re-minting, no-relocation-id error path, child renumbering).
- New end-to-end test: two clones mint the same ID, the managed sync worker integrates and pushes, both beads survive, worktree clean.
- `cargo test -p sase_core` all green; `cargo fmt` + `clippy -p sase_core --all-targets` clean.
- `just check` passes, full suite **25785 passed, 7 skipped**.

One note: an earlier `just check` failed the slow-tools PNG snapshot and the bead lock-timeout contention test. Both were host-contention flakes — a second full `just check` was running concurrently in another workspace (that run took 17m44s vs 5m51s clean). Both pass in isolation and in the clean rerun; I recorded the recurrence as a `+1` on the existing bead `sase-cx` rather than filing a duplicate.

The pre-existing `sase-core-rs>=0.17.15,<0.18.0` window warning is unrelated to this change and left alone; the facade's fallback covers wheels without the new binding.

Bead is confirmed closed. Now committing — starting with the linked `sase-core` repo.

`sase-core` is clean and in sync. Now the main workspace.

Both repos are committed, clean, and in sync with their upstreams.

**`sase-core`** — `fix(bead): relocate duplicate bead ids instead of failing the merge`
The union merge in `crates/sase_core/src/bead/events.rs` now tracks per-event provenance, detects duplicate `issue_created` events, and relocates the loser (root subtree → free ID, child → next free sibling), remapping IDs and re-minting `event_id`s. Winner selection is orientation-independent. Exposed as `merge_bead_event_streams_with_relocation` plus `BeadEventStreamMergeWire` through the pyo3 binding; the original function keeps its signature and error behavior.

**`sase`** — `fix(bead): recover sync when two clones mint the same bead id`
`conflict_resolver` allocates relocation IDs from a store-wide pool, writes and stages the relocated stream, and reports `relocated duplicate beads: <old> -> <new>`. The facade falls back to the legacy binding on older wheels. Adds the end-to-end regression test.
